statements.text: Additionally, we must continue to pursue Artificial Intelligence to ensure the United States remains ahead of the curve in this powerful driver of innovation, economic growth and opportunity while also being a leader in accountability and developing a high standard of AI ethics. Artificial Intelligence has the potential to change our day-to-day lives, which means we need strong and thoughtful federal regulation. In the absence of a robust federal framework, states should be able to regulate AI based on the needs of their communities.
statements.venue: Campaign website, 'AI, Tech, and Innovation' priorities page

statements.text: We must also advance strict regulation as it pertains to the safety of kids, teens, and vulnerable populations, ensuring chatbots and other AI tools are built with safety top of mind. Export controls on the advanced AI chips are also critical to ensure that AI is developed in America, for the benefit of Americans.
statements.venue: Campaign website, 'AI, Tech, and Innovation' priorities page

statements.text: Finally, with the advancement of Artificial Intelligence, we must prioritize working people and their employment. AI groups should work hand in hand with labor leaders to ensure the work force and our economy handles AI integration to the benefit of working class Americans, not just corporations and billionaires.
statements.venue: Campaign website, 'AI, Tech, and Innovation' priorities page

statements.text: Organizations must also be required to disclose pertinent information as it relates to data centers, their environment and community impact, and job opportunities before being allowed to open and operate in communities. While prioritizing working people, data centers should provide ample job training for local workers, rather than outsourcing jobs and leaving our communities out of the fold.
statements.venue: Campaign website, 'AI, Tech, and Innovation' priorities page

statements.text: I join a majority of the general public in wanting restrictions or moratoriums as we assess the actual and potential negative consequences. However, we must first rebuild trust in agencies gutted of the expertise and public servants to provide honest guidance, transparent oversight and effectively implemented guardrails.
statements.venue: Patch (Homewood-Flossmoor) candidate questionnaire on data centers

statements.text: Studies substantiate the correlation between AI and “intellectual laziness,” loss of human decision-making, discerning truth from lies or information from propaganda. Most troubling to me is how AI can incorporate and contribute to historic social ills, particularly in disproportion use against people of color.
I would definitely argue the need to regulate AI use in the public sector, if we are to maintain any trust in, efficacy and/or fair application of governmental resources.

I lean towards the hybrid approach of “cooperative federalism”: establishing a strong federal floor of essential safety, privacy, and fairness standards, to create a predictable baseline for all; preserving the right of states to legislate further, allowing them to address unique local concerns and serve as laboratories for more ambitious regulatory ideas; ideally leveraging the strengths of both systems, creating a cohesive national strategy that honors the traditional and vital role of states in protecting their residents.

In addition to my previous comments on AI, I would protect the right of communities to determine whether and how data centers might benefit their communities, including cost-benefit analyses and environmental studies.
